v.rationale:
All three pass their own suites (19, 22 and 11 tests). All three get the core side-effect contract right: points are incremented inside the transaction and the email goes out through DB::afterCommit. My probes confirmed nothing is sent and no points are added when an outer transaction or a nested savepoint rolls back.

impl-1 and impl-2 are almost identical: an atomic conditional-UPDATE claim, a policy with route-level authorization, and a FormRequest. impl-1 ranks first for three reasons:
- It keeps OrderAlreadyShipped as a plain domain exception and maps it to 409 in bootstrap/app.php. impl-2 makes the model throw a Symfony HTTP exception.
- It uses the fluent ->can() route method.
- It has a test that a failed shipment insert rolls everything back.

impl-2 adds app-wide exception and middleware config and some ceremony (Http::preventStrayRequests). Its tests are slightly broader, but that doesn't make up for the HTTP coupling.

Both share a latent policy bug: when is_staff isn't loaded on the User instance, the policy throws a TypeError and returns 500. Real requests load the user from the DB, so in practice this mostly affects tests.

impl-3 uses lockForUpdate, which is also sound. It ranks last because it:
- maps 409 with a try/catch in the controller
- puts staff authorization in the FormRequest instead of a policy
- adds foreign keys to #[Fillable]
- leaves the caller's model dirty after both success and failure (the probe confirmed it)
- deletes the base example tests
- has thinner tests, with no datasets and no stale-instance or 404 cases
